We derive an exact feedback-delay threshold for a single payload spin from the phase information in the pilot record. On a finite menu of control phases, the pilot record enters the minimum-error update decision only through the direction of its first circular moment when that moment is nonzero. This result motivates a controller that estimates the direction from orthogonal pilot measurements and retains the existing phase whenever the predicted gain is lost to diffusion. For finite spin ensembles, we bound the distinguishability of the photon-count distributions in terms of optical readout and carrier-phase uncertainty, including fluctuations shared across spins. Packet simulations at matched spin budgets show that gated feedback can improve reliability with a single readout channel. With independently readable quadratures and sufficient spin preparations, decision-directed software tracking achieves lower packet error without a hardware phase update.
item.dc:creator: Amirhossein Taherpour, Abbas Taherpour, Mazen Hasna, Tamer Khattab, Khalid Qaraqe

item.title: Dynamical quantum codes and logic gates on a lattice with sparse connectivity
item.description: arXiv:2510.05225v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce several dynamical schemes that take advantage of mid-circuit measurement and nearest-neighbor gates on a lattice with maximum vertex degree three to implement topological codes and perform logic gates between them. We first review examples of Floquet codes and their implementation with nearest-neighbor gates and ancillary qubits. Next, we describe implementations of these Floquet codes that make use of the ancillary qubits to reset all qubits every measurement cycle. We then show how switching the role of data and ancilla qubits allows a pair of Floquet codes to be implemented simultaneously. We describe how to perform a logical Clifford gate to entangle a pair of Floquet codes that are implemented in this way. Finally, we show how switching between the color code and a pair of Floquet codes, via a depth-two circuit followed by mid-circuit measurement, can be used to perform syndrome extraction for the color code.
item.dc:creator: Dominic J. Williamson, Bence Het\'enyi

item.title: Decoding Multimode Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Codes with Noisy Auxiliary States
item.description: arXiv:2510.12677v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In order to achieve fault-tolerant quantum computing, we make use of quantum error correction schemes designed to protect the logical information of the system from decoherence. A promising way to preserve such information is to use the multimode Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) encoding, which encodes logical qubits into several harmonic oscillators. In this work, we focus on decoding the measurements obtained from Steane-type quantum error correction protocols for multimode GKP codes. We propose a decoder that considers the noise present on the auxiliary states, more specifically by tracking the correlations between errors on different modes spreading throughout the error-correction circuit. We show that leveraging the correlations between measurement results and the actual error affecting the multimode GKP state can decrease the logical error probability by at least an order of magnitude, yielding more robust quantum computation.
item.dc:creator: Marc-Antoine Roy, Thomas Pousset, Baptiste Royer

item.title: Rotational Asymmetry beyond Phase Rigidity in Non-Hermitian Eigenfunctions
item.description: arXiv:2512.18856v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Phase rigidity, the standard measure of eigenvector nonorthogonality, vanishes at an exceptional point (EP). We show that this collapse need not imply phase spreading and can mask persistent phase organization. Using quantum and classical relative entropies linked by the Holevo bound and the phase--Fourier entropic uncertainty relation, we uncover rotational asymmetry within this organization. In both a classical microcavity and quantum hydrogen, phase entropies peak and Fourier entropies dip on a broad parameter scale. Near the EP, one branch gains rotational asymmetry while the other loses it despite common rigidity loss. Changes in quantum rotational asymmetry dominate those in classical asymmetry, consistent with the weak-pattern scaling of the uncertainty gap. This hidden phase organization predicts testable probe-induced splitting axes relevant to EP sensing and allows distinct rotational asymmetries at fixed geometric imaginarity. Rotational asymmetry thus reveals non-Hermitian eigenfunction structure beyond nonorthogonality.
item.dc:creator: Kyu-Won Park, Soojoon Lee, Kabgyun Jeong

item.title: Approximate Decoherence, Recoherence and Records in Isolated Quantum Systems
item.description: arXiv:2601.19703v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using the framework of decoherent histories, we study which past events leave detectable records in isolated quantum systems under the realistic assumption that decoherence is approximate and not perfect. Using tools from quantum state discrimination, we establish asymptotically for a large class of (pseudo-)random histories how the strength of decoherence changes the number of reliable records, i.e., we quantitatively answer the question: when can approximate decoherence be approximated by exact decoherence? In addition, we reveal a clear decoherence structure for long histories based on a numerically exact solution of a random matrix model that, as we argue, captures generic aspects of decoherence. In particular, we observe strong recoherences for maverick histories that are statistical outliers with respect to Born's rule. From the perspective of the Many Worlds Interpretation, our results reveal a "branch selection problem" and shed light on the emergence of Born's rule and the theory confirmation problem.
item.dc:creator: Philipp Strasberg, Joseph Schindler, Jiaozi Wang, Andreas Winter

item.title: Detailed, interpretable characterization of mid-circuit measurement on a transmon qubit
item.description: arXiv:2602.03938v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mid-circuit measurements (MCMs) are critical components of the quantum error correction protocols expected to enable utility-scale quantum computing. MCMs can be modeled by quantum instruments (a type of quantum operation or process), which can be characterized self-consistently using gate set tomography. However, experimentally estimated quantum instruments are often hard to interpret or relate to device physics. We address this challenge by adapting the error generator formalism -- previously used to interpret noisy quantum gates by decomposing their error processes into physically meaningful sums of "elementary errors" -- to MCMs. We deploy our new analysis on a transmon qubit device to tease out and quantify error mechanisms including amplitude damping, readout error, and imperfect collapse. We examine in detail how the magnitudes of these errors vary with the readout pulse amplitude, recover the key features of dispersive readout predicted by theory, and show that these features can be modeled parsimoniously using a reduced model with just a few parameters.
item.dc:creator: Piper C. Wysocki, Luke D. Burkhart, Madeline H. Morocco, Corey I. Ostrove, Riley J. Murray, Tristan Brown, Jeffrey M. Gertler, David K. Kim, Nathan E. Miller, Bethany M. Niedzielski, Katrina M. Sliwa, Robin Blume-Kohout, Gabriel O. Samach, Mollie E. Schwartz, Kenneth M. Rudinger

item.title: The emergence of classical stochasticity
item.description: arXiv:2602.04633v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We examine the emergence of classical stochasticity for a quantum system governed by a Pauli-type master equation. It is well-known that while such equations describe the evolution of probabilities, they do not automatically justify reasoning based on the assumption that the system exists in a definite state at intermediate times. On the other hand, we show that this assumption is crucial for the standard calculation of stochastic times such as the persistent time and the time of first arrivals. It is also curious to point out that the standard derivation of the Pauli master equation based on the Fermi Golden Rule actually proceeds by assuming that the system remains in a definite state as the starting point to derive the transition rate to a different state. By studying the so-called ultradecoherence limit, we show that the Pauli master equation can also be arrived at without such an assumption. Instead, that the system exists in a definite state has to be justified by a different argument. We then consider examples of single particles, bosons, and fermions in the ultradecoherence limit to illustrate how classical stochasticity may emerge from quantum mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Xuan Du Trinh, Isma\"el Septembre, Hai-Chau Nguyen

item.title: Scalable testing of quantum error correction
item.description: arXiv:2602.04921v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The standard method for benchmarking quantum error correction is Monte Carlo sampling. However, direct estimation of rare logical failures through unconditional Monte Carlo sampling can be prohibitively expensive, even with efficient simulators such as stim. In this paper, we present a scalable approach that combines stratified fault injection with extrapolation. Our insight is that some of the fault space can be sampled efficiently, after which extrapolation is sufficient to complete the testing task. As a result, our tool scales to distance 17 for a physical error rate of 0.0005 with a two-hour time budget on a desktop, while Monte Carlo sampling using \stim observed 0 logical errors at distance 13 with the same time budget. At distance 17, ScaLER estimated a logical error rate of $1.51 \times 10^{-11}$ with high confidence.
item.dc:creator: John Zhuoyang Ye, Jens Palsberg

item.title: Instance-optimal high-precision shadow tomography with few-copy measurements: A metrological approach
item.description: arXiv:2602.04952v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the sample complexity of shadow tomography in the high-precision regime under realistic measurement constraints. Given an unknown $d$-dimensional quantum state $\rho$ and a known set of observables $\{O_i\}_{i=1}^m$, the goal is to estimate expectation values $\{\mathrm{tr}(O_i\rho)\}_{i=1}^m$ to accuracy $\epsilon$ in $L_p$-norm, using possibly adaptive measurements that act on $O(\mathrm{polylog}(d))$ number of copies of $\rho$ at a time. We focus on the regime where $\epsilon$ is below an instance-dependent threshold. Our main contribution is an instance-optimal characterization of the sample complexity as $\tilde{\Theta}(\Gamma_p/\epsilon^2)$, where $\Gamma_p$ is a function of $\{O_i\}_{i=1}^m$ defined via an optimization formula involving the inverse Fisher information matrix. Previously, tight bounds were known only in special cases, e.g. Pauli shadow tomography with $L_\infty$-norm error. Concretely, we first analyze a simpler oblivious variant where the goal is to estimate an observable of the form $\sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_i O_i$ with $\|\alpha\|_q = 1$ (where $q$ is dual to $p$) revealed after the measurement. For single-copy measurements, we obtain a sample complexity of $\Theta(\Gamma^{\mathrm{ob}}_p/\epsilon^2)$. We then show $\tilde{\Theta}(\Gamma_p/\epsilon^2)$ is necessary and sufficient for the original problem, with the lower bound applying to unbiased, kurtosis-bounded estimators when $p \geq 1$. Our upper bounds rely on a two-step algorithm combining coarse tomography with local estimation. Notably, $\Gamma^{\mathrm{ob}}_\infty = \Gamma_\infty$. In both cases, allowing $c$-copy measurements improves the sample complexity by at most $\Omega(1/c)$. Our results establish a quantitative correspondence between quantum learning and metrology, unifying asymptotic metrological limits with finite-sample learning guarantees.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Proceedings of Thirty Ninth Conference on Learning Theory, PMLR 336:1115-1185, 2026
item.dc:creator: Senrui Chen, Weiyuan Gong, Sisi Zhou

item.title: Light-Matter Interactions Beyond the Electric Dipole Approximation in Extended Systems Without Multipole Expansion
item.description: arXiv:2603.10271v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a general theoretical framework to capture light-matter interactions beyond the electric-dipole approximation, applicable to extended materials interacting with spatially structured electric fields without truncation at finite multipolar order. The approach is based on the Power-Zienau-Woolley (PZW) Hamiltonian for light-matter interactions and a representation of the material Hamiltonian in a basis of maximally localized Wannier functions (MLWFs). We utilize this novel approach to clarify the limitations of the ubiquitous dipole approximation. We consider electric fields with both uniform and non-uniform intensity profiles and a range of ratios of system size to the wavelength of light. We identify the precise conditions under which the dipole approximation breaks down, leading to significant errors in the light-induced dynamics. Contrary to conventional belief, we find that the dipole approximation is robust for uniformly illuminated 1D or 2D materials if light propagates perpendicular to the material. For 3D materials or non-perpendicular illumination, the dipole approximation starts to break down when the wavelength of light becomes comparable to the system size. Furthermore, the dipole approximation fails to capture the light-matter interaction when the material is illuminated partially or non-uniformly. For slowly varying field intensities this failure can be corrected by the finite-order multipolar corrections. However, for fields that vary substantially over the system size, correcting via finite order multipolar terms becomes computationally impractical. In contrast, our approach captures the beyond-dipole light-matter interactions at a computational cost of a standard dipole calculation. This efficiency paves the way for accurate first-principles simulations of spatially-structured light-matter dynamics in nanoscale devices, quantum materials, and interfaces.
item.dc:creator: Rishabh Dora, Roman Korol, Vishal Tiwari, Rahul Chourasiya, Ignacio Franco

item.title: Hybrid Analog-Digital Simulation of the Abelian Higgs model
item.description: arXiv:2603.12391v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To investigate gauge theories with near-term quantum computers warrants exploration of nontraditional quantum simulators to find resource-efficient simulation protocols and ultimately access exotic features of different field theories, including unexplored regimes of the QCD phase diagram. In this work, using superconducting transmon qutrit processors, we formulate and implement a pulse-based, three-level, hybrid analog-digital simulation protocol of the (1+1) dimensional Abelian Higgs model (AHM) on two sites. Alongside this approach, we experimentally realize a gate-based implementation of the same model. Using the natural mapping of the three-level truncation of the transmon Hilbert space to the spin-1 truncated AHM, we observe real time dynamics of AHM field observables, which are analogous to electric field operators, with both protocols. For the analog-digital protocol, we engineer a Floquet simulation with a combination of local analog drives, driven modification of the natural interaction Hamiltonian of the two transmons, and dynamical decoupling pulses. For the digital protocol, we use a state-of-the-art qutrit processor to implement a Trotterized simulation of the model incorporating advanced error mitigation techniques. We further discuss the scalability of the two approaches, and their potential to be extended to the simulation of other model Hamiltonians. Our experiments demonstrate a viable platform for future studies of spin-1 and SU(3) based gauge theory models on current and near-term transmon qutrit processors.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Asaduzzaman, Rayleigh W. Parker, Noah Goss, Ahmed I. Mohamed, Max Neiderbach, Zane Ozzello, Ravi K. Naik, Alexander F. Kemper, Irfan Siddiqi, Yannick Meurice, Machiel S. Blok

item.title: Scalable quantum resources with short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains
item.description: arXiv:2603.17071v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range or power-law couplings that decay too quickly for this purpose. We demonstrate that two spin-$\tfrac12$ chain models -- a staggered nearest-neighbor XXX chain and a long-range XXZ chain -- develop an effective OAT nonlinearity when projected onto the symmetric sector. We show that these dynamics generate metrologically useful spin-squeezed states and Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger coherences that ensure violation of many-body Bell inequalities. We confirm the accuracy of this mapping by comparing it to the exact dynamics and demonstrate that the generated correlations can be read out using a single probe qubit. The resulting dynamics can be simulated with analog and digital quantum simulators.
item.dc:creator: Marcin P{\l}odzie\'n, Jan Chwede\'nczuk

item.title: Fermionic entanglement and quantum correlation measures in molecules
item.description: arXiv:2604.07633v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze fermionic entanglement and correlation measures in the ground and the low temperature thermal state of the water molecule as a function of the internuclear distance in the context of the full configuration interaction approach. The aim is to obtain a general entanglement based characterization of the electronic eigenstates. We consider first the spin-up - spin-down partition and the associated Schmidt decomposition, examining the total up-down entanglement of the electronic wave function. We then consider the one- and two-body entanglement derived from the one- and two-body reduced density matrices (DMs), which measure the deviation of the state from a Slater determinant (SD). All blocks of these DMs are examined. We also introduce and analyze new measures like the up-down two-body mutual information, which measures the up-down correlation at the two-body level, and two types of two-body negativities, the latter detecting and measuring the "inner" entanglement of the reduced two-body DMs, i.e., their deviation from a convex mixture of SDs. Finally, the dissociation limit is also analyzed, considering both the exact ground state (GS) as well as the thermal state in the zero temperature limit, representing the projector onto the "GS band" of almost degenerate lowest lying eigenstates.
item.dc:creator: J. Garcia, J. A. Cianciulli, R. Rossignoli

item.title: Learning Cut Distributions with Quantum Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2604.14381v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The probabilistic nature of quantum computation can be an asset rather than an obstacle for combinatorial optimization. In this work, we tackle the problem in which the sampled distribution itself is the object being optimized. This perspective is especially natural for fairness, coverage, and robustness objectives, where success is determined by the least-protected components rather than by average or best performance. We develop this idea by learning graph cut distributions. The resulting framework turns Fair Cut Cover into a native quantum distribution-learning problem and uses quantum circuits as trainable generators of cut distributions. We prove that standard QAOA at depth one achieves higher Fair Cut Cover values than optimal Semidefinite programming plus Gaussian hyperplane rounding on complete graphs with at least four vertices. We further establish a separation on a family of high-girth graphs using published QAOA evaluations, compare against a classical column-generation heuristic in numerical experiments, and examine finite-sampling and noise effects in quantum hardware implementations. These results suggest a broader role for this type of quantum algorithms: not merely finding good bitstrings, but learning useful combinatorial distributions for worst- and average-case-aware optimization.
item.dc:creator: Bao Bach, Cameron Ibrahim, Reuben Tate, Jad Salem, Stephan Eidenbenz, Ilya Safro

item.title: Coherence Transfer in Quantum Networks
item.description: arXiv:2604.17196v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Detecting coherence transfer in complex quantum networks is challenging under uncharacterized experimental conditions and with limited access to the system. Here, we use the coexistence of static and dynamic coherence to derive a nonlinear criterion for coherence transfer. The criterion applies even when the verification capabilities of checkpoint nodes are uncharacterized. It requires only minimal one-network output analysis, up to the number of output state dimensions. Each output requires only two-setting measurements of state populations, regardless of the network size. The criterion is general for both spatial and temporal networks, including those with multiple coherence sources, and applies to quantum transport in solid-state nanostructures. Experimentally, using entanglement swapping, we transfer polarization-entangled pairs in four- and six-photon entanglement networks. The criterion provides experimental evidence of coherence transfer in multiphoton entanglement networks. Our findings provide a practical tool for investigating the presence, role, or function of coherence transfer in quantum networks.
item.dc:creator: Chun-Yang Lin, Yu-Cheng Li, Shih-Hsuan Chen, Sheng-Yan Sun, Ching-Jui Huang, Kuan-Jou Wang, Che-Ming Li

item.title: Quantum Fisher Information and Separable Energy Minima in Spin Systems
item.description: arXiv:2605.03022v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a general method to bound the minimum energy of spin Hamiltonians over separable states with fixed single-particle reduced density matrices. The method uses a two-particle optimization and identifies conditions under which the resulting bound is tight. For ferromagnetic Ising and Ising-like interactions on any regular graph, we obtain an exact separable-energy minimum expressed through the quantum Fisher information (QFI) of the local state; a symmetric separable state attains the optimal correlation on every bond. For fully connected ferromagnetic Ising-like systems, ground-state correlations give a lower estimate of this single-particle QFI with a rigorous O(1/N) finite-size error. Further exact results relate symmetric-separable minima of antiferromagnetic Ising-like and XY-like models to local expectation values, and ferromagnetic spin-1/2 Heisenberg chains to quantum fidelity. We also derive bounds for separability across fixed partitions into contiguous blocks.
item.dc:creator: G\'eza T\'oth, J\'ozsef Pitrik

item.title: ffsim: faster simulation of fermionic quantum circuits
item.description: arXiv:2605.03123v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present ffsim, an open-source software library for fast simulation of fermionic quantum circuits. ffsim exploits conservation of particle number and the z component of spin, symmetries present in a wide range of fermionic systems, to dramatically reduce memory usage and simulation time compared to general-purpose quantum circuit simulators. Compared to FQE, a library with similar functionality, ffsim differs in software design and is faster on a representative set of simulation benchmarks. Beyond state vector evolution by basic fermionic gates, ffsim offers a number of additional features including variational ansatzes, Hamiltonian time evolution via Trotter-Suzuki product formulas, efficient sampling of Slater determinants, seamless integration with Qiskit and PySCF, and comprehensive documentation. We demonstrate ffsim's capabilities on scientific applications, including a 64-qubit Hubbard model with 8 electrons. ffsim's source code and documentation are available via https://github.com/Qiskit/ffsim.

item.title: Unified entropy entanglement
item.description: arXiv:2605.22150v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The unified entropy as a generalization of the von Neumann entropy exhibits distinct diversity which contains the Tsallis entropy, the R\'{e}nyi entropy, the von Neumann entropy as special cases. The unified-($r,t$) entropy entanglement with $0<r<1$ and $0< t\leq 1$ was shown to be an entanglement monotone in literature. In this paper, we explore unified-($q,s$) entropy entanglement with $q>1$ and $qs\geq1$ and show that it is also an entanglement monotone and that both of them are monogamous. Going further, we present a global multipartite entanglement measure (GlMEM) based on the unified entropy and it has two subclasses which are classified by the parameters $(q,s)$ and $(r,t)$. Consequently, from the view of the complete multipartite entanglement measure theory, we show that one of them is a complete multipartite entanglement monotone and is not only completely monogamous but also tightly completely monogamous, but the other one is even not complete. We also explore the genuine entanglement measures induced by the unified entropy and the relations with the bipartite entanglement and the global entanglement are discussed, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Wenxue Ren, Binghao Li, Ruiqun Niu, Yu Guo, Shuanping Du

item.title: Minimum-Length Permutation-Invariant Qudit Codes from Edge-Colorings of Complete Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2605.22439v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study permutation-invariant quantum codes in the symmetric subspace $\mathrm{Sym}^n(\mathbb{C}^q)$ of $n$ qudits of local dimension $q$. For every integer $q\ge 2$, we construct a permutation-invariant code with parameters $((4,q,2))_q$. Thus four physical qudits suffice to encode one logical qudit with distance two in the symmetric sector for every local dimension. We also show, using a self-contained decoupling and rank argument, that no permutation-invariant code of dimension $q$ and distance at least $2$ exists in $\mathrm{Sym}^n(\mathbb{C}^q)$ for $n\le 3$. Hence four qudits are necessary and sufficient. The construction has simple representation-theoretic and combinatorial descriptions. On $\mathrm{Sym}^4(\mathbb{C}^q)$, the distance-two Knill--Laflamme conditions split into root and Cartan parts. By restricting supports to the even-entry occupation layer, all root-error conditions vanish automatically. The remaining Cartan conditions reduce to linear balancing constraints on packets of occupation vectors. These packets admit a natural graph-theoretic interpretation in terms of the vertices and edges of the complete graph $K_q$: for odd $q$, they are organized by the midpoint rule, while for even $q$, they are organized by a decomposition of $K_q$ into perfect matchings. In this way, the existence of minimum-length $((4,q,2))_q$ permutation-invariant codes is reduced to a parity-dependent edge-coloring problem on $K_q$.
item.dc:creator: Eric Kubischta, Ian Teixeira

item.title: Poincar\'e sphere representation of spin-driven polarization encoding in two-dimensional perovskite light sources
item.description: arXiv:2605.28695v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Nonlinear optical light sources enable the generation of photons with polarization states that are intrinsically determined by underlying material dynamics, rather than imposed through external modulation. Here, we investigate how four-wave-mixing signal fields emitted by a representative two-dimensional perovskite system can be leveraged for polarization-encoded quantum communication. The experimentally reconstructed signal field is represented by Stokes-vector trajectories on the Poincar\'e sphere to establish a predictive framework that connects the optical response to practical figures of merit for spin-driven semiconductor light sources. Applied to a model quantum communication scheme in the weak coherent-state regime, this representation quantifies the resolution of the polarization states generated at two pump-probe delays, thereby enabling estimation of the number of detected photons per decoded bit. In addition, a microscopic model connects the signal-field ellipticity to spin relaxation within the exciton fine structure, revealing that interference between resonantly enhanced optical transitions governs the accessible polarization states. The analysis suggests that modest stabilization of the lowest-energy biexciton could substantially improve polarization-encoding performance, offering a route toward materials optimization. More broadly, these results motivate closer integration of nonlinear spectroscopy, semiconductor materials, and quantum information science in the development of novel light sources for quantum communication.
item.dc:creator: Zijian Gan, Shuyue Feng, Camryn J. Gloor, Wei You, Andrew M. Moran

item.title: Fourier analysis of quantum neural network with non-linear data embedding
item.description: arXiv:2606.14206v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fourier analysis has become a crucial tool for understanding the expressivity of Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC) models, as well as an important indicator of barren plateaus. While existing literature has only studied angle-embedded VQCs in a noiseless environment, here we develop the Fourier analysis of VQCs with non-linear data embedding, with particular focus on amplitude embedding, as it provides a naturally compact encoding scheme. We first investigate a difference in the domain of input features that leads to a distinct expressivity of the zero-frequency Fourier coefficient. Assuming that the unitaries generated from the parameter space forms at least a unitary 2-design, we derive that, in integer-valued frequencies, the mean of the Fourier coefficients is concentrated at zero, and the variance is upper bounded by an inverse power-law function with respect to the infinity norm of the frequency. A numerical evidence of exponentially decaying pattern with respect to the frequency magnitude is also established, providing a frequency-perspective of viewing VQC model expressivity and its trainability. When a noise channel with unitary Kraus operators and probabilities $\{p_k\}$ is taken into account, the variance is further suppressed by a factor $\left(\sum_kp_k^2\right)^{Q}<1$ for $Q$ as the number of channel instances applied. Furthermore, we demonstrate and validate the analytical results through simulations, both noiseless and noisy, and contrast its expressivity against the angle-embedded Fourier features. We also examine the model's performance where target functions contains non-integer frequencies. Our results establish a rigorous Fourier framework for amplitude-encoded VQCs, offering both theoretical guarantees on expressivity, hence trainability scaling in the frequency domain, as well as practical simulations for deployment on noisy quantum devices.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Haiyue Kang et. al. Quantum Sci. Technol. 11 0450d7 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Haiyue Kang, Martin Sevior, Muhammad Usman

item.title: Quantum Computing Algebra (QCA), the theory and implementation
item.description: arXiv:2606.17621v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a real geometric algebra framework designed for the direct translation of the Dirac formalism into geometric algebra representations. Unlike previous approaches based on positive-definite signatures, QCA employs a split-signature construction that enables a natural realization of quantum states and operators while simplifying computational implementation. We further present an implementation of QCA using the \textit{GAALOP} software and show how quantum gates and multi-qubit systems can be efficiently represented and generated computationally. As an application, we demonstrate the use of QCA in quantum game theory, where the real-algebraic formulation provides computational advantages for modeling entangled strategies and quantum interactions. The proposed framework establishes a practical bridge between the abstract formalism of quantum computation and efficient geometric algebra implementations.
item.dc:creator: Jaroslav Hrdina, Dietmar Hildenbrand, Oliver Rettig

item.title: From spectral structure to sensing limits in quantum thermometry
item.description: arXiv:2606.25933v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The precision of a quantum thermometer is fundamentally constrained by the spectral structure of the probe itself, and a systematic mapping between the configurations of energy levels and thermometric performance provides relevant information to design optimized devices. In this work, we establish such a mapping by analyzing a broad class of quantum systems, ranging from finite spin ensembles and degenerate atoms to confining potentials, quantum walks, and continuous-spectrum models. We derive exact scaling laws for the quantum Fisher information, revealing two distinct high-temperature universality classes: finite-spectrum probes exhibit a $T^{-4}$ decay, while unbounded or continuous spectra yield a slower $T^{-2}$ decay. At low temperatures, we show that sensitivity, though universally exponentially suppressed, can be enhanced arbitrarily by engineering degenerate excited states or a quantum walk on a fully connected topology. By contrast, specific quantum walk topologies provide a distinct enhancement mechanism based on gap engineering, whereby an optimal network size yields an optimized $T^{-2}$ low-temperature scaling. Furthermore, power-law spectra enable tunable scaling of thermometric performance with system size, offering a design principle for optimal probes in specific temperature windows. Our results contribute to transform spectral information into a resource for quantum thermometry, providing both fundamental bounds and practical guidelines to tailored temperature sensing.
item.dc:creator: Youssef Aiache, Simone Cavazzoni, Abderrahim El Allati, Paolo Bordone, Matteo G. A. Paris

item.title: A broadband, individually addressable 2D-3D photonic integrated circuit for trapped-ion qubit control
item.description: arXiv:2607.25062v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Trapped ions provide a high-fidelity platform for quantum information processing, yet delivery of multiple, distinct wavelengths across large networks of interaction zones remains a bottleneck. Conventional free-space light delivery lacks scalability, while on-chip grating couplers suffer from narrow operational bandwidth that increases circuit footprint and optical interfacing complexity. Here we show a broadband photonic integrated circuit capable of addressing individual ion locations. The circuit combines a planar waveguide lens with a micromirror fabricated using two-photon polymerization at wafer scale. Optical characterization demonstrates three individual addressing spots from $\lambda = 405$- $880\,\mathrm{nm}$ with $-25\,\mathrm{dB}$ average intensity crosstalk at $5\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ pitch. We trap $^{40}\mathrm{Ca}^{+}$ above the mirror to demonstrate preferential repumping and utilize $^{138}\mathrm{Ba}^{+}$ ions to characterize optical crosstalk far away from the mirror. Charging of the dielectric and silicon structures currently limits a full experimental demonstration of the devices' capabilities but could be mitigated in future designs. This monolithic photonic architecture could bring broadband addressing in an on-chip modality to trapped-ion technology. More broadly, combining additive manufacturing with established quantum device fabrication techniques could open new possibilities for implementing advanced quantum architectures.

item.title: A loss-limited optimum for fixed uniform multi-pass quantum sensing per absorbed photon
item.description: arXiv:2608.25534v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multi-pass schemes send a photon through a sample several times to learn more about it. When the sample rather than the light is scarce, the natural figure of merit is the information gained per photon the object absorbs. We show that three properties fix the loss-limited optimum of every fixed scheme in which a single photon passes repeatedly and uniformly through the sample and is detected once at the end: a payoff that grows as the square of the pass number, the same survival probability on every pass, and no dose from a photon already lost. They force a single trade-off function $h(x)=x^2/(e^x-1)$, where $x$ is the number of passes times the loss per pass. Its maximum, 0.648, sits at $x_{\rm opt}=1.594$. The multi-pass optima of Koppell and Kasevich and of Yu et al. are two instances, and the loss-limited ceiling of interaction-free interrogation is a third when its payoff is counted as conclusive detections. Phase sensing of a weakly absorbing object is optimal at $m_{\rm opt}=x_{\rm opt}/(\epsilon+\alpha)$ passes; the absorption $\alpha$ and the parasitic loss $\epsilon$ enter the optimum only through their sum, but the damage counts only $\alpha$. N00N states and their loss-robust generalisations do worse per absorbed photon, and optimising over photon and pass number returns a single recycled photon; Gaussian probes and chains tailored pass by pass lie outside this class and can exceed its ceiling by a bounded factor. Absorption estimation gains nothing, for any scheme. Above the crosstalk crossover of the mode sorter, detecting a faint companion below the Rayleigh limit costs the companion a dose independent of its faintness; below it, and under direct imaging at any separation, the dose grows without bound as the companion fades. Among single photons and path-entangled number states, the gentlest measurement of a fragile sample is also the simplest: a single photon, recycled.
item.dc:creator: Christoph F. Wildfeuer

item.title: Extended Wigner's Friend Scenarios with Agent-like Observers on Quantum Computers
item.description: arXiv:2609.12527v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Wigner's friend thought experiment raises the question of whether quantum theory can be applied consistently to systems that include observers. Extended Wigner's Friend Scenarios include spatially separate observers sharing entanglement. In the Local Friendliness (LF) framework, these scenarios lead to experimentally testable inequalities derived from Absoluteness of Observed Events and Local Agency, assumptions weaker than those needed for Bell inequalities. Their violation therefore has stronger implications, but LF tests are more experimentally challenging because they require an observer implemented as a quantum system. Drawing from the literature on artificial intelligence, we implement the "friend" with explicit agent-like functionality in a reversible quantum circuit. The agents store measurement outcomes, condition subsequent operations on stored information, and, in the most structured case, use Born-rule probabilities to bet on outcomes of their own future observations based on past observations. We study the circuits through ideal simulations, simulations using an IBM-device noise model, and experiments on the IBM processor ibm_marrakesh. Ideal simulations reproduce the maximal quantum violation of an LF inequality up to finite-shot fluctuations, while hardware runs show positive LF violations for all agents. These results are a step towards more sophisticated agent-like observer models in LF experiments on quantum computers. By focusing on functionality rather than size alone, this approach complements tests of quantum theory in the macroscopic regime and opens a direction for studying agents whose use of quantum theory is implemented within coherently controlled quantum dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Laux, Eric G. Cavalcanti

item.title: Indistinguishability Theory for Identical Particles with Invariant Degrees of Freedom
item.description: arXiv:2609.14428v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Identical particles have dynamically invariant labels in all setups where their degrees of freedom can be partitioned into two parts, which we call internal and visible, with the visible part subject to unitary evolution, while the dynamically invariant internal part accounts for the partial distinguishability of particles. We give the explicit form of the visible state in terms of the indistinguishability function, generalizing the standard symmetrization/antisymmetrization postulate for bosons/fermions with internal modes. The indistinguishability function on the symmetric group accounts for the permutation symmetry of the dynamically invariant label state and gives a self-contained description of the symmetry spectrum of the visible state. It is shown that the indistinguishability of single particles emitted independently from a stable source is completely characterized by the projective measures on the symmetry spectrum. We reveal a hierarchy of successive upper bounds on the projective measure of indistinguishability in terms of marginal projective measures. We point out an experimentally feasible way to get the upper bounds on the indistinguishability of an arbitrarily large number of single photons by direct experimental readout of their marginal projective measures. We also analyze the indistinguishability of coherent superpositions and convex mixtures and resolve a recently posed problem.
item.dc:creator: Valery Shchesnovich

item.title: Ancilla-assisted multi-qubit quantum gates with polar molecules
item.description: arXiv:2609.18972v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum error correction enables reliable quantum computation using imperfect physical gates, but its implementation often requires multi-qubit controlled-unitary gates $\text{C}_{\mathbb{N}}(U)$ acting on $\mathbb{N} \ge 3$ qubits. Their direct realization is challenging, while decomposing them into standard one-qubit and two-qubit gates can increase circuit depth and error rates. Here, we present an ancilla-assisted scheme to directly implement $\text{C}_{\mathbb{N}}(U)$ in optically trapped ultracold polar molecules. By appropriately selecting qubit states for the ancilla and data qubits, dark states can appear during two smooth $\pi$ pulses. This can generate a controlled-phase gate with the phase set by the relative phase between the pulses; notably, a single $2\pi$ pulse yields a $\text{C}_{\mathbb{N}}(Z)$ gate. Numerical analysis for a simple molecular spatial configuration demonstrates that the gate infidelity is dominated by qubit decoherence, yielding a $\text{C}_2(Z)$ fidelity of $0.996$ estimated with $T_2^\ast=1.5$~s and a gate duration of $T \approx 4\text{~ms}$. Furthermore, diabatic errors remain low, on the order of $10^{-4}$ for $\mathbb{N}=2,3$ and $10^{-3}$ for $\mathbb{N}=4$, even with dipole-dipole interaction strengths as low as $25\hbar/T$.
item.dc:creator: Yan Lu, Xiao-Feng Shi

item.title: Anomalous Hardening of a Fluctuation-Induced Gap
item.description: arXiv:2609.34416v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a mean-field picture, a gap opened by quantum fluctuations grows with them. This can fail if the fluctuating mode is critical and its displacement compensates its coupling to the degenerate states. A single parameter sets the gap response: above a universal threshold, the gap hardens as the critical fluctuations weaken. Whenever the parameter is nonzero, overcompensation beyond the critical point drives a secondary phase transition. In a quantum Rabi ring with synthetic flux, exact diagonalization shows the gap of a photonic Landau level rising by 15% as the critical variance falls by 25%.
item.dc:creator: Shu He, Liwei Duan

item.title: Quantum-echo Markov process for combinatorial optimization
item.description: arXiv:2609.38943v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a quantum-echo Markov process for combinatorial optimization. Quantum dynamics based on quantum annealing (QA) or the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is used to engineer the transition kernel. Increasing the annealing time in QA or the number of layers in QAOA enables transitions to explore distant configurations while suppressing large energy changes. The Hamming-space delocalization originates from operator spreading, whereas the energy-space localization arises from a dynamically generated correlation. For optimization, we propose quantum-echo local optimization. For the ferromagnetic Ising chain, increasing the annealing time or circuit depth yields a nearly quadratic improvement in the dependence of the mean first-passage time on the inverse optimality gap compared with random single-spin flips. For the random Ising model, increasing these parameters initially improves optimization performance, whereas further increases degrade performance in QA and lead to saturation in QAOA. Quantum-echo greedy descent substantially improves the performance, highlighting the complementary roles of quantum dynamics in exploration and greedy descent in exploitation. These results establish quantum-echo dynamics as a framework for engineering structured transition kernels and provide a route to using finite-resource quantum many-body dynamics as a computational primitive for iterative optimization.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuhiko Shirai

item.title: Analytic construction of dimension-dependent steering witnesses from generalized equiangular measurements
item.description: arXiv:2610.07314v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we construct a dimension-dependent family of generalized equiangular measurements (GEAMs) that gives explicit steering witnesses in every prime dimension $d$. The construction consists of \(d-1\) mutually unbiased measurements and an additional normalized family of \(2d-1\) Hermitian operators, which is a $(1,2d-1)$-POVM {(POVM denotes a positive, operator-valued measure).} For odd prime dimensions, we reduce the noncentral operators to three-dimensional invariant subspaces and solve the central operator in a two-dimensional subspace. We combine complementary Gershgorin bounds from two unitarily equivalent matrix representations to obtain a fully analytic asymmetric interval for {a parameter} that guarantees positivity. The {qubit and qutrit cases} are treated separately. Finally, using a maximally entangled realization and the local-hidden-state bound for GEAMs, we obtain an explicit steering inequality and a sufficient criterion for quantum violation in every prime dimension.
item.dc:creator: Adam Rutkowski, Katarzyna Siudzi\'{n}ska

item.title: Finite-time quantum equilibration from local correlations
item.description: arXiv:2610.16351v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study equilibration of a fixed subsystem coupled to an initially maximally mixed bath. We show that the worst-input mean-square error, maximised over observation windows of length $T$, is bounded from above and below by the mean square of a complete local autocorrelation on $[0,T]$. The constants depend only on the subsystem dimension, and no assumption on degeneracies of energies or energy gaps is required. Subtracting the stationary part of the correlation gives equilibration to the temporal state; retaining it gives thermalisation to the maximally mixed state. We then obtain explicit bounds for two static Hamiltonian families. A periodic spin-clock model thermalises on $O(n\log n)$ windows at fixed accuracy despite an exponentially small positive energy. A randomly dressed commuting model, with interaction range $O(\log N)$, has expected error $O(N^{-b}+T^{-1})$ while retaining an extensive family of conserved observables. We explain how the locally weighted spectrum determines these bounds.
item.dc:creator: Piotr \'Cwikli\'nski

item.title: $\mathsf{EFI}\Leftrightarrow\mathsf{1PRS}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.18799v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A series of recent works has established EFI pairs as the "minimal" assumption for quantum cryptography. Recently, Cavalar et al. [CCC+26] showed that EFI pairs are equivalent to non-uniform expanding single-copy pseudorandom state generators (1PRS), and obtained a non-uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. We remove the non-uniformity in their construction and prove that EFI pairs are equivalent to expanding 1PRS. As a corollary, we obtain the first uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. Together with the equivalence of statistically verifiable one-way state generators and commitments proved by Batra and Jain [BJ24], this gives a quantum analogue of the classical equivalence between one-way functions, commitments, and pseudorandom generators.
item.dc:creator: Rishabh Batra

item.title: Geodesic Efficiency of Counterdiabatic Charging in a Quantum Battery
item.description: arXiv:2610.32610v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate an open quantum battery consisting of a resonator acting as the energy-storage unit, a frequency-tunable two-level system acting as a controllable mediator, and an external coherent drive serving as the energy source. In the dispersive regime, the dynamics reduce to those of a driven harmonic oscillator with a tunable effective coupling. Starting from the vacuum state, the resonator remains in a coherent state under a Lindblad master equation describing photon leakage at zero temperature. We derive a counterdiabatic (CD) driving protocol that compensates for dynamical lag and ensures that the system follows the prescribed reference trajectory. As a result, the energy stored in the resonator increases monotonically without transient oscillations, allowing the battery to reach the target ergotropy at the prescribed final time $t_f$. The CD trajectory follows a geodesic in the coherent-state phase space and achieves near-unity geodesic efficiency over a broad range of pulse durations, whereas unassisted charging exhibits markedly lower efficiencies. Finally, we show that the CD protocol saturates the quantum speed limit for the charging process.
item.dc:creator: F. Ahmadi, S. Salimi

item.title: QDMin: Coherent Quantum Minimum Finding over Parametrized Many-Body Hamiltonians
item.description: arXiv:2610.40320v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many questions about interacting quantum systems ask which member of a Hamiltonian family $H(\mathbf{q})$ has the lowest ground-state energy, rather than for the ground state of one Hamiltonian. A pointwise scan answers this with one many-body solve per candidate. QDMin (Quantum Deformation Minimum Finding) instead holds all $N_q$ candidates in a coherent register and searches them with a ground-energy threshold oracle, replacing $N_q$ solves by $O(\sqrt{N_q})$ coherent oracle calls. We identify static-field (Hubbard-Stratonovich) families as a broad class in which this minimum is a rigorous variational bound that the parent ground state does not reveal, and we make the oracle robust to imperfect ground-state preparation by fixed-point amplitude amplification. The measured search constant places the crossover against a pointwise quantum scan at $N_q \approx 220\xi^2$, where $\xi$ is the overhead of a coherent call. We test the search on realistic sd-shell (USDB) static quadrupole landscapes with up to $10^6$ grid points and on a Hubbard ring with competing orders. It pays where competing minima trap local descent, needing about four times fewer energy queries than multistart descent for oblate-prolate coexistence in $^{28}$Si, and not on smooth single-well landscapes. Circuit-level simulations validate the complete pipeline on a schematic model. The gain concerns the number of energy queries; any advantage of the quantum solver itself is separate.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek, P. Arumugam

item.title: Open Quantum Time Crystals without External Thermodynamic Resources: Go and No-Go Theorems
item.description: arXiv:2611.09540v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Time crystals are phases of matter that spontaneously break time-translation symmetry. They have been ruled out in the ground and Gibbs states of isolated systems with only short-range interactions, yet they have been proposed and observed experimentally in nonequilibrium settings such as Floquet and open systems. However, existing proposals for time crystals in open quantum systems require an external supply of thermodynamic resources, such as work or energetic coherence. Whether coupling to an environment, without any such resource supply, can activate a time crystal absent in the isolated system remains open. We answer this question systematically through a Go theorem and a no-go theorem. The Go theorem answers it affirmatively: we construct an explicit model in which coupling a system to a zero-temperature Gibbs environment via a time-independent, energy-conserving interaction, with only short-range Hamiltonians, activates a time crystal in a stationary state that shows none in isolation. This coupling reproduces a Lindblad master equation satisfying three conditions---time-independent Hamiltonian and jump operators, time-translation covariance, and detailed balance---that hold in standard derivations unless thermodynamic resources are supplied externally. The no-go theorem shows that, for every Lindblad master equation satisfying these conditions and every stationary state, dissipation can never contribute to activation; only an environment-induced Hamiltonian term can. Indeed, the periodic two-time correlation function of any such time crystal coincides with that of the isolated system with the open-system Hamiltonian, the sum of the bare isolated Hamiltonian and the environment-induced Hamiltonian, in the thermodynamic limit. These results reveal both the possibility and the origin of time crystals in open systems without external resource supply.
item.dc:creator: Yuri Ogami, Hiroyasu Tajima

item.title: Local Quantum Metrology: Precision Limits for Observers in QFT
item.description: arXiv:2611.17948v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: How precisely can an observer estimate a parameter related to a quantum field? This question is answered for quantum-mechanical systems using the SLD--Bures--Fisher metric and the quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound. However, local algebras in relativistic quantum field theory are of type III: they carry no trace, so that states are not described by density matrices in the algebra, and they have no pure normal states, such that the SLD quantum Fisher information and the quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound cannot be defined in the usual way. We define the SLD (Bures) quantum Fisher information on arbitrary von Neumann algebras through Uhlmann's transition probability and prove a quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound for collective measurements. We also show that the bound is sharp, and equals the largest classical Fisher information obtainable by measurements in the region.
item.dc:creator: Markus Fr\"ob, Albert Much

item.title: Witnessing Magic (and other Quantum Resources)
item.description: arXiv:2611.19017v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by measurements of quantum magic, we study the sampling cost of resource robustness ---a quantifier for a broad class of quantum resources--- by bounding the variance of optimal robustness witnesses. We first lower bound the samples required to estimate a state's resource robustness using Cram\'er-Rao bounds. We find that the number of measurements scales at least quadratically in the robustness for highly mixed states, and at least linearly in the generalized robustness for broad families of pure states, making it difficult to measure either robustness to low absolute error when the states are highly resourceful. We then derive two complementary bounds in terms of the geometry of witnesses, one of which is tight for a class of resource theories including coherence and bipartite entanglement. An additional hurdle occurs for tracking the onset of resource robustness along state-space trajectories: the integrated witness variance along a path is at least the squared resource gain over Fisher length, indicating that a state evolution with exponential resource gain necessarily goes through states for which the robustness cannot be measured efficiently. This hurdle does not occur when estimating robustness to fixed relative, rather than absolute, error. These results suggest that the ideal witness-based resource estimation task, for general resource theories, is the estimation of generalized robustness to low relative error on highly resourceful pure states.
item.dc:creator: Brian Barch, Luis Pedro Garc\'ia-Pintos

item.title: Observable Spectral Framework for Noisy Amplitude Amplification: Stopping Stability and Correction
item.description: arXiv:2611.20622v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Stopping rules for noisy amplitude amplification often rely on channel-specific success-probability formulas, limiting their transfer across noise mechanisms. We develop an observable spectral framework for stationary noisy standard amplitude amplification with a known ideal success fraction, under explicit leading-mode, spectral-separation, and residual-control conditions. Within this class, the first amplification lobe has a damped-oscillatory leading component and a bounded non-leading contribution. We derive how frequency shift, damping, and observable phase offset displace the leading peak, and establish sampled-gap criteria for retaining the ideal integer stopping depth, certifying recalibration, or selecting a robust candidate window. In single-target Grover search, frequency and damping errors have stopping-coordinate sensitivities proportional to the search-space size, whereas phase offsets scale with its square root; residual modes can independently reverse the ordering of neighbouring depths. Analytical constructions, circuit simulations, finite-shot inference, and calibration-derived device-like trajectories examine these predictions and their operational limits. For a 64-element search, an a posteriori sampled-set check selects depth five over six, with success probability increasing from 0.595 to 0.626. The resulting theory links observable spectral dynamics to conditional integer stopping guarantees without requiring a separate microscopic channel solution.
item.dc:creator: Ge Zhong, Charith Jayasekara, Nisal De Silva, Muhammad Usman, Muhammad Aamir Cheema, Chetan Arora

item.title: Complex quasiprobabilities as measurable temporal interference
item.description: arXiv:2611.22643v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum dynamics can encode interference information that conventional correlation functions leave unresolved. Here we show that the imaginary component of the extended Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability reveals dynamical distinctions absent from out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) formed from two repeated Hermitian observables at infinite temperature. We interpret its real and imaginary components as complementary quadratures of interference between many-body echo amplitudes. We prove that the imaginary component vanishes for every unitary evolution if either projective measurement has two outcomes, whereas nonreal values arise for generic unitary dynamics when it has at least three (e.g., spin-1 systems). We develop an algorithm to reconstruct the full quasiprobability from covariances of local probe signals over repeated preparations of randomised initial states, using forward evolution and probe readout only. In a spin-1 chain, a nonzero imaginary signal distinguishes a real Hamiltonian $H$ from $-H$ despite identical corresponding OTOCs, and identifies opposite sides of a pair-conversion resonance at short times while dipolar and quadrupolar OTOCs remain nearly unchanged. These results show how temporal interference resolves dynamical ambiguities and provides additional constraints for Hamiltonian inference.
item.dc:creator: Wenzheng Dong, Alexander Yosifov, Jinzhao Sun

item.title: Gutzwiller Quantum-Classical Embedding for Dynamics Simulations of Correlated Electron Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.24592v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Simulating the real-time dynamics of correlated electron systems requires a nonperturbative treatment of local correlations over long times, a challenge for classical methods. We present the time-dependent Gutzwiller quantum-classical embedding framework, t-GQCE, for generic multi-orbital lattice models with time-dependent Hamiltonians. Within the time-dependent ghost Gutzwiller approximation, a noninteracting quasiparticle lattice propagated classically is coupled to finite interacting embedding models propagated on quantum processors. The two parts exchange only embedding Hamiltonian parameters and single-particle density matrices, and the framework is agnostic to the quantum solver. We demonstrate it with adaptive variational quantum dynamics simulations of interaction quenches in the Hubbard model on the Bethe lattice. Without ghost orbitals, the embedding problem reduces to a single qubit, simulated on IBM quantum hardware with an ancilla qubit. With ghost orbitals, t-GQCE suppresses the artificial undamped oscillations of the conventional Gutzwiller approximation and approaches nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory results for weak and strong quenches. Statevector simulations with 2 to 6 ghost orbitals per spin, or 8 to 16 qubits, give adaptive circuits that follow the embedding states with infidelities below $5\times10^{-4}$. Under trapped-ion noise models, circuit compression, measurements in rotated orbital bases with post-selection, and noise mitigation reduce the errors two- to threefold. At one third of the error rates of a hardware-benchmarked noise model, they reach an absolute accuracy of $0.01$ for all single-particle density matrix elements and the double occupancy with $10^5$ shots per time step, and the Quantinuum H2-Emulator gives similar accuracy, suggesting that t-GQCE is a viable approach for early fault-tolerant quantum processors.

item.title: Photon number correlations in harmonics driven with classical and quantum light
item.description: arXiv:2611.28498v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent reports of nonclassical intensity correlations in harmonic generation raised questions about whether strong harmonic correlations necessarily imply genuinely quantum behaviour. Here, we compare the low-photon-number perturbative harmonic generation driven by classical and bright squeezed vacuum sources. The latter generates strong auto- and cross-correlations in the harmonic spectrum. Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and heralding measurements show that the cross-correlations are fully classical and can be explained by the common fluctuations from the driving field. A visible scaling of the measured correlation function with mean harmonic flux is observed, which is well-explained by a click detector-response model.

item.title: Topological subregions in Chern Simons theory and topological string theory
item.description: arXiv:2511.08746v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The standard, gapped entanglement boundary condition in Chern Simons theory breaks the topological invariance of the theory by introducing a complex structure on the entangling surface. This produces an infinite dimensional subregion Hilbert space, a non-trivial modular Hamiltonion, and a UV-divergent entanglement entropy that is a universal feature of local quantum field theories. In this work, we appeal to the combinatorial quantization of Chern Simons theory to define a purely topological notion of a subregion. The subregion operator algebras are spaces of functions on a quantum group. We develop a diagrammatic calculus for the associated $q$-deformed entanglement entropy, which arise from the entanglement of anyonic edge modes. The $q$-deformation regulates the divergences of the QFT, producing a finite entanglement entropy associated to a $q$-tracial state. We explain how these ideas provide an operator algebraic framework for the entanglement entropy computations in topological string theory \cite{Donnelly:2020teo,Jiang:2020cqo, wongtopstring}, where a large- $N$ limit of the $q$-deformed subregion algebra plays a key role in the stringy description of spacetime.

item.title: Quantum fields in a cold atomic simulator: relaxation and phase locking in tunnel-coupled 1D bosonic quasi-condensates
item.description: arXiv:2512.13901v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider a prime example of simulating interacting relativistic QFT with cold atoms: the realisation of the sine-Gordon model by tunnel-coupled quasi-1D Bose gases. While experiments have shown that it can realise the sine-Gordon model in equilibrium, studies of non-equilibrium dynamics have revealed phase-locking behaviour that contrasts with predictions from sine-Gordon field theory. Here, we examine a one-dimensional field-theoretic model of the system and find that the phase-locking behaviour can be understood in terms of the longitudinal harmonic trap, and that the additional degrees of freedom observed in the experiment do not appear to play a significant role. Therefore, the experimental setup provides a good simulator of the sine-Gordon quantum field theory, even out of equilibrium, if the inhomogeneous background induced by the trap is taken into account. Furthermore, our results support the idea that modifying the longitudinal trap to a box shape should result in agreement with standard sine-Gordon dynamics. The main remaining open issues are accounting for 3D corrections and modelling the effect of the boundaries.

item.title: Floquet Engineering of a Quasiequilibrium Superradiant Phase Transition in Landau Polaritons
item.description: arXiv:2604.08635v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Superradiant phase transitions (SRPTs), characterized by photon condensation and macroscopic matter polarization, are forbidden in equilibrium for homogeneous fields by no-go theorems. Here, we show that Floquet driving can circumvent this constraint in a Landau polariton system consisting of a two-dimensional electron gas coupled to a terahertz cavity in a DC magnetic field. An off-resonant AC magnetic field modulates the cyclotron frequency and light--matter coupling strength while leaving the diamagnetic term unchanged, generating an additional DC coupling contribution. This drives the system across a critical threshold into a superradiant phase, characterized by photon condensation and Landau-level polarization in the ground state of the Floquet Hamiltonian. This quasiequilibrium approach offers a route to SRPTs distinct from driven-dissipative schemes.

item.title: Supergravity flows, wormholes and their pseudo-Hermitian holographic duals
item.description: arXiv:2605.16168v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We find solutions to consistent truncations of supergravity where some real scalars are analytically extended to imaginary values, ensuring the metric remains real-valued. Among the solutions there are Lorentzian traversable wormholes connecting two asymptotically anti-de Sitter spacetimes and flows that have a real metric also when uplifted to ten or eleven dimensions. We argue that the holographic duals are pseudo-Hermitian and $PT$-symmetric theories. Wormhole solutions also admit an interpretation as the low-energy theory of two stacks of branes and anti-branes after tachyon condensation. The wormhole is then dual to an entangled state of two copies of the theory that lives on a stack of branes. We present some evidence by computing the mutual information between the theories at each boundary and by identifying the Goldstone bosons associated with the breaking of the two copies of Poincar\'e symmetry to their diagonal subgroup.

item.title: Inner sublattice competition: a minimal mechanism for reentrant localizations in Aubry-Andr\'e lattice
item.description: arXiv:2606.24720v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a double mosaic Aubry-Andr\'e (DMAA) model with two independent quasiperiodic potentials assigned to corresponding even and odd sublattices of the AA lattice, and show that the competition between them gives rise to multiple localization-delocalization transitions under single-parameter tuning. Such reentrant localizations are verified by comprehensive numerical characterizations including the inverse participation ratio, normalized participation ratio, fractal dimension, and real-space wavefunction distributions. Simulations based on a continuous polariton model yield consistent results, confirming the experimental feasibility of the predicted phenomena. This inner sublattice competition mechanism works in a minimal way for reentrant localizations without additional ingredients or dynamical modifications such as long-range hopping, mixed quasiperiodic and random disorder, or non-Hermitian gain and loss, offering a concise route to engineer reentrant localization based on the canonical AA lattice family.

item.title: Revealing precision bounds on neutrino oscillation parameters with quantum estimation theory
item.description: arXiv:2606.28275v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum estimation theory provides ultimate precision bounds on parameter estimation, independent of experimental setups. In this article, we apply this theoretical framework to neutrino oscillations, aiming to clarify some subtle issues and reveal the maximum achievable precision of oscillation parameters. First, taking the example of two-flavor oscillations, we clarify how the quantum Fisher information (QFI) depends on the choice of bases when the basis transformation itself involves the parameters in question. Then, for three-flavor oscillations, we compute the QFI matrix for electron and muon neutrino states in the flavor basis and derive analytical expressions and numerical results for both diagonal and off-diagonal elements. The implications of off-diagonal correlations for multiparameter estimation are discussed, including the compatibility of optimal measurements, the Holevo bound, and the spectral analysis of the QFI matrix, from which we show that a single neutrino channel leaves exactly two parameter combinations unconstrained. The quantum Cram\'{e}r-Rao bounds on the precision of oscillation parameters for typical reactor and long-baseline accelerator neutrino experiments are obtained as vacuum, state-level benchmarks, which establish a theoretical reference for the ultimate precision achievable in future neutrino oscillation experiments.

item.title: Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains
item.description: arXiv:2607.09511v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Majorana zero modes provide a route to fault-tolerant qubits by encoding information non-locally in fermion parity. Their sensitivity to noise is expected to decrease exponentially with increasing separation between the Majoranas, a suppression known as topological protection. Kitaev chains engineered in quantum dot-superconductor arrays provide a tunable platform in which separated Majorana zero modes can emerge at the ends of the chain, even in two-site chains. These minimal-chain modes are known as poor man's Majoranas and retain characteristic Majorana properties, including near-zero energy and equal electron-hole character, but have only limited protection. A key outstanding challenge is to move beyond identifying such modes in electrical transport measurements and achieve coherent qubit control in the time domain. Here, we demonstrate a Majorana parity qubit by realizing coherent coupling between two-site Kitaev chains. Since total fermion parity is conserved, the system separates into global even and odd parity manifolds. We observe coherent parity oscillations in both manifolds with equal oscillation frequencies at the Majorana sweet spot, as predicted for isolated Majorana zero modes. We further show that the oscillation frequency and coherence depend systematically on inter-chain coupling and quantum-dot detunings, in close agreement with our model for short, partially protected chains. Our results establish the first coherent control of a Majorana qubit, encoded in the fermion parity of Majorana zero modes in minimal Kitaev chains.

item.title: Qubit-qubit-qutrit quantum correlations in $H \to f \bar f V$
item.description: arXiv:2607.26122v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We perform an extensive analysis of the quantum correlations carried by the qubit--qubit--qutrit pure state arising in the decay of a massive scalar into a fermion--antifermion pair and a massive gauge boson, $H \to f \bar f V$, specialising to the Higgs boson decay $h \to \tau^- \tau^+ Z$. Working with the exact tree-level spin state and its systematic expansion around the massless-fermion limit, we obtain analytic control over the entire phase space: the bipartite entanglement measures, the genuine $2 \otimes 2 \otimes 3$ entanglement structure (the Miyake classification), as well as the Bell-inequality violations and the non-stabiliserness (magic) are all mapped and reproduced by compact formulas. The bipartite measures exhibit a monogamy-like trade-off between the fermion pair and the fermion--boson pairs. The state is genuinely $2 \otimes 2 \otimes 3$ entangled over almost the entire phase space, most strongly in the collinear regions. We derive, for the first time, semi-analytical expressions for the tight $4 \times 4 \times 2$ Bell inequalities of the $2 \otimes 2 \otimes 3$ system, generalising the optimisation previously available only for three qubits, and find that the local-hidden-variable bound is violated over the entire phase space, reaching within a few per cent of the quantum bound at the upper endpoint of the di-tau mass spectrum. We further extend the stabiliser R\'enyi entropy and the non-local magic to systems with unequal local dimensions, and show that the near-endpoint state carries almost exactly one bit of non-local magic, which peaks at $\log_2 \frac{27}{7} \simeq 1.95$ in the collinear regions. The differential decay rate concentrates precisely in the most nonclassical region of the phase space.

item.title: PyCC: A Reference Quantum Chemistry Python Package for Education, Validation, and Rapid Prototyping
item.description: arXiv:2610.04107v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: PyCC is a Python-based quantum chemistry package that emphasizes coupled cluster and related methods. Developed over the last five years, PyCC's purpose is to provide a clear reference implementation that will serve as a validation suite for production code, a platform for rapid prototyping and testing of new methods, and an educational resource for newcomers to the field. The package covers both closed- and open-shell single-determinant references in spatial- and spin-orbital formulations for the coupled cluster hierarchy through triples-including methods such as CC3, as well as for MP2 and CI methods. PyCC provides a broad range of molecular properties such as analytic first and second energy derivatives including gradients, Hessians, polarizabilities and atomic polar tensors, as well as non-energy-derivative properties, such as velocity-gauge atomic polar tensors and diagonal Born-Oppenheimer corrections, plus dynamic linear response functions, and excitation energies. The package includes a number of unique capabilities, such as real-time CC propagation (up through CC3), atomic axial tensors for simulating vibrational circular dichroism spectra at the MP2, CID, CISD, and CCSD levels, and local correlation methods including perturbation-aware correlation domains. The code is designed around a shared Wavefunction base and a method-agnostic derivative layer that enables a new method to inherit the full energy-derivative property set once it supplies its reduced densities and their first-order responses. PyCC is fully open source and available on GitHub under the BSD 3-clause license.

item.title: Adding Temperature to the Adiabatic Connection: Hybrid Functionals for Static and Dynamic Correlation
item.description: arXiv:2610.22284v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Capturing static and dynamic electron correlation simultaneously at manageable computational cost remains a key challenge in electronic structure theory. Motivated by the recurring role of effective temperature in self-consistent field methods we extend the adiabatic connection mechanism from density functional theory (DFT) to include a temperature dimension. The formalism unifies established hybrid functionals with information-density matrix functional theory (i-DMFT) and thermally-assisted-occupation DFT, clarifying their theoretical basis and the respective prescriptions for the temperature parameter. It further gives rise to thermally enhanced hybrid functionals, in which static correlation is captured via fractional occupations generated by an effective "correlation temperature" within thermal Hartree-Fock, while dynamic correlation is described by established density functional approximations. We assess the performance of several thermally enhanced hybrids for different cases where i-DMFT was previously shown to fail. Furthermore, we discuss and test different schemes for determining the correlation temperature and investigate the accuracy of different such choices for a benchmark set of different organic molecules. The results clarify the achievable balance of accuracy, generality, and efficiency, establishing thermally enhanced hybrids as a systematic route toward low-cost treatment of both correlation types.

item.title: Entanglement Distribution in Quantum Switch Networks: Memory Limits and Achievability
item.description: arXiv:2610.28596v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the minimum persistent memory required to distribute a graph state through a quantum switch. Specifically, consider a central switch that assists $n$ remote users in distributing a graph state, using independently generated user-switch Bell pairs. Since Bell-pair generation is probabilistic, different links generally succeed at different times. When a Bell pair is generated, the qubits may need to be stored in memory while waiting for other links to succeed. Recently, new protocols have been proposed to reduce this storage overhead by processing and releasing some switch qubits before all Bell links are available. However, these protocols do not characterize the minimum persistent switch memory required at each stage. Moreover, the local-cover method in the state-of-the-art Piecemaker protocol is computationally expensive for general target graphs. In this work, we characterize the minimum persistent switch memory required after any subset of users' Bell links are generated and processed. We then develop an online stabilizer-transition protocol that attains this limit, which can be implemented in polynomial time in the number of qubits $n$ and does not require information about future Bell-link successes. Moreover, when one Bell link succeeds per round of duration $\Delta t$, for the path graph $P_n$, Piecemaker requires the cumulative switch-qubit storage time $\Theta(n^2\Delta t)$ and peak memory of at least $\left\lfloor n/2 \right\rfloor$ \textit{for any arrival order}, while under some arrival orders, our protocol requires only $(n-1)\Delta t$ and retains just one persistent switch qubit. More generally, for tree graphs, our protocol can reduce the $\Theta(n^2\Delta t)$ cumulative storage time in Piecemaker to $O(n\log n\,\Delta t)$ for some arrival orders.
