item.title: Enhanced SiV-phonon coupling in dissipation-diluted diamond nanomechanics
item.description: arXiv:2610.39271v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Solid-state color centers embedded into mechanical resonators, where orbital states mediate interactions between spins and long-lived phonons, are a promising platform for hybrid quantum systems. The negatively charged silicon vacancy center in diamond (SiV-) is particularly favorable for strain-coupling to nanomechanical resonators because of its large spin-strain susceptibility and compatibility with device integration. Tensioned nanomechanical resonators offer an attractive route due to their ultra-long mechanical coherence times enabled by diluting defect-induced dissipation, though it is unclear if the same dilution effect undermines strain-mediated coupling to material defect centers. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a tensioned diamond nanobeam platform that enables enhanced strain coupling to SiV- orbital states. Through monitoring the optical response of the SiVs to the static and dynamical strain of the mechanical resonator, we observe that dynamical strain localizes near the clamps of these resonators under static strain. This allows us to enhance SiV-mechanical coupling and the mechanical coherence simultaneously, and provide a SiV-strain sensitivity with greatly improved accuracy over previous literature values. Thus, our work opens a pathway towards seconds-long coherence hybrid quantum systems utilizing point defects in diamond nanomechanics for quantum information processing.
item.dc:creator: Guanhao Huang, Amberly Xie, Chang Jin, Evelyn Hu, Marko Lon\v{c}ar

item.title: Quasi-particle sector hybridization and the onset of chaos in spin ladders
item.description: arXiv:2611.19053v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: How quasiparticle numbers influence the emergence of quantum chaos is a fundamental question in interacting many-body systems. We investigate this interplay in a spin-$1/2$ XXZ ladder, where the strong-rung regime supports an approximate organization of many-body eigenstates into quasi-particle(triplon) number sectors. Using spectral statistics, triplon-based observables, and von Neumann entanglement entropy, we characterize the microscopic hybridization of triplon-number sectors as the leg coupling increases. We find that the crossover toward Gaussian orthogonal ensemble statistics shifts to weaker couplings with increasing system size, whereas the characteristic crossover scale associated with triplon-sector hybridization exhibits a much weaker size dependence. Furthermore, eigenstate-to-eigenstate fluctuations exhibit scaling consistent with the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis even while remnants of the strong-rung structure persist, suggesting that spectral chaos does not necessarily require complete sector hybridization.
item.dc:creator: Arnav Pushkar, Abhik Kumar Saha

item.title: An isolated complex Hadamard matrix with nonzero defect
item.description: arXiv:2611.20136v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The defect of a complex Hadamard matrix is the real dimension of the solution space obtained by linearizing the row orthogonality equations in the phases of the entries, with the first row and column fixed. It is known that defect zero implies isolation up to Hadamard equivalence. The converse, whether every isolated complex Hadamard matrix has defect zero, was open and is the square-matrix case of a conjecture of Banica, Ozteke and Pittau. We answer this question in the negative. We exhibit a Butson-type Hadamard matrix of order 13 with entries among the sixth roots of unity and show that it is isolated and has defect one. We prove isolation by showing that no nonzero solution of the linearized equations satisfies the second order condition obtained by the second author for directions of convergence of sequences of Hadamard matrices. In the language of commuting squares of matrix algebras, the example shows that an isolated commuting square can fail the span condition introduced by the second author as a sufficient condition for isolation.
